newsitem.title: USA: D&P places MCI debt on rating watch-up.
newsitem.headline: D&P places MCI debt on rating watch-up.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it placed the debt ratings of MCI Communications Corp on rating watch-up based on the company's announced merger with British Telecommunications plc.
Currently, MCI's senior unsecured debt is rated single-A and commerical paper is rated D-one by D&P.

Credit protection measures at MCI remain very strong within its current rating category, D&P said in a statement. The merger with BT should result in capital expenditure and cost savings as well as greater financial resources to expand MCI's local telephony subsidiary, MCI Metro, it said.

Balancing these benefits will be the size of MCI's share buyback program, which will be completed prior to the closing of this merger, and continued investment in high-growth, capital intensive areas. Another concern is the ultimate capital structure of the merged companies and the resulting level of debt from the cash portion of the BT offer to MCI shareholders and the special dividend to BT shareholders prior to the closing, it said.

MCI is the second largest long distance provider in the United States. BT provides local and long distance telecommunications throughout the United Kingdom. BT holds a 20 percent ownership stake in MCI.
The combined company, Concert, is projected to have revenues of $42 billion and cash flows of about $12 billion.
